source.title: Scaling Laws for Generative Mixed-Modal Language Models
source.authors: Armen Aghajanyan; L. Yu; Alexis Conneau; Wei-Ning Hsu; Karen Hambardzumyan; Susan Zhang; Stephen Roller; Naman Goyal; Omer Levy; Luke Zettlemoyer

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model size and training-token count and fits held-out-loss scaling laws using the Hoffmann et al. parameterization, extending the measurement to additional modalities and mixed-modal models.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted uni-modal scaling-law parameters, mixed-modal scaling results, and a Speech|Text test of a predicted competition barrier. Figures 1–4 show additional scaling curves. Results cited from Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. are not treated as this study's results. The study's batch-size, training-flatness, stability, and tokenizer findings are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits the Hoffmann et al. (Chinchilla) loss form E + A/N^α + B/D^β with the same Huber/L-BFGS procedure to its own sweeps of 8M–6.7B parameters × 5B/10B/100B tokens. It does this for text (OPT data) and six other token modalities, then fits an additive mixed-modal extension. It also checks one extrapolation to a 30B Speech|Text run. The text fit is a same-method replication (T1); the other modalities and the mixed-modal fits are new settings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that uni-modal scaling dynamics differ sharply across modalities. They say the Speech|Text prediction 'does hold' at 30B parameters and 50B tokens, crossing the competition barrier.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Hoffmann et al. loss parameterization and fitting procedure as a basis, then adds terms for interactions between modalities. The study uses causal masking for its main experiments and reports a causal-objective comparison in the appendix.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted scaling coefficients vary substantially by modality and modality pairing. The causal masked versus standard causal objective comparison for Speech and Text yields parameters described as close to identical.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-modal interaction terms (α_i,j, β_i,j) correlate with training flatness, optimal batch size and gradient-spike counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling-law fit parameters predict training dynamics and hyperparameters.

record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty intervals for fitted parameters. The explicit large-scale test concerns the Speech|Text competition barrier rather than a numerical prediction of the 30B run's loss; the reported 30B test is one pairing. Mixed-modal fitted parameters are plotted rather than tabulated in the text provided.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 1–2's training curves and modality-by-size perplexity plots are represented by the aggregate fitted-law rows. Figures 6–9's optimization flatness, batch-size, and gradient-spike analyses are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions. Appendix tokenizer reconstruction and speech-tokenizer evaluation results are also outside the claim.

untested.parts: Only about 3 orders of magnitude in N and 1.3 in D (three token budgets). No compute-axis law and no fit-quality check.
Extrapolation across orders of magnitude; numeric loss prediction for a single-modality text model.
Not tested. The 6ND minimisation is used only to place the competition barrier, not to give a loss-optimal allocation versus compute.
Not tested. Shape co-varies with size (Table 2).
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
Not tested. There are no downstream tasks.
Parameter counting, schedule, fitting method (beyond a changed Huber δ), data choice within a modality, and curvature away from a power law.

missing.what: The Text fit is called 'similar to those reported by Chinchilla', with a different dataset. Chinchilla's own fit (α≈0.34, β≈0.28) differs markedly from α=0.18, β=0.22, which is relevant to V7's point that published laws disagree. The authors also raised the Huber δ above Chinchilla's (a fitting-method change).
Figure 5 also plots 350M and 2.7B Speech|Text ratios against the predicted barrier (smaller models stay in competition). This should be part of the R15 extrapolation evidence.
Figure 4 shows extrapolated bi-modal laws with experimental points for four pairings.

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty or goodness-of-fit is reported for any fit. The token range is narrow (three budgets). The modalities are all tokenized sequences from a shared decoder setup, so V5 support covers token-based generative modelling only. The comparison with Chinchilla's published coefficients rests on the original source's values, not this paper's numbers.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests losses across its stated modalities, model sizes, and token counts, not every language-model setup or a broader range beyond the reported sweeps.
The 30B Speech|Text experiment checks whether a predicted competition barrier is crossed, not whether small-run loss fits predict the larger run's loss.

The study calculates a compute-optimal point for breaking the Speech|Text competition barrier, not the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute or how both quantities grow with compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study covers text, image, speech, code, molecules, and selected pairings; it does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream-task performance is related to scale or pretraining loss.

The study compares causal masked and standard causal objectives for Speech and Text, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting method, nor test whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: 30B Speech|Text model
rows.operation_detail: Train the predicted large Speech|Text configuration and compare its perplexity with the mean of the two unimodal models.
rows.measure: Ratio of mean unimodal Speech and Text perplexity to Speech|Text perplexity; below 1 indicates the competition barrier is crossed
rows.baseline: 0.5 × (Speech perplexity + Text perplexity), divided by Speech|Text perplexity
rows.value: The ratio crosses below 1; numerical value figure only
rows.note: The authors state that the prediction holds and that the 30B model crosses the competition barrier.
rows.check: This is an extrapolation test, so it bears on V2, not V5. Laws fitted on ≤6.7B runs predicted a 30B run (about 4.5× larger, less than one order of magnitude). The prediction is a threshold (perplexity ratio below 1); Figure 5 plots a predicted final ratio, but no numeric agreement is reported. The predicted optimum was N=28.35B, D=45.12B; the run used 30B parameters and 50B tokens.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V2 as written. Predicted barrier configuration: N=28.35B, D=45.12B; tested configuration: 30B parameters, 50B tokens. Authors report a barrier crossing; no numerical absolute-loss prediction error is stated.
source_check.problem: A threshold crossing at about 4.5 times the largest fitting model does not establish absolute-loss prediction orders of magnitude beyond the fitting runs.

relation.reason: The study fits scaling laws to its own parameter/data sweeps and tests a predicted competition-barrier crossing.

tranche.reason: The uni-modal experiments reuse the Hoffmann loss parameterization, Huber fitting and L-BFGS initialization procedure, with a changed Huber parameter; the bi-modal experiments extend that method.

source_check.notes: Figure 5's stated ratio and below-one criterion are internally inconsistent with the usual direction of perplexity improvement; R15 reproduces the source. Main experiments use causal masked CM3 training; ordinary causal training is the Appendix A.2 control.

statements.correction: Supplied source: arXiv v1, 10 January 2023. Table 1: Text α/β=0.18/0.22; Image=0.13/0.13; Image-Text=0.12/0.11. Appendix A.2: controlled objective comparison. No coefficient intervals or quantitative goodness-of-fit diagnostics reported.
statements.problem: The coefficients, objective control and lack of quantitative fit diagnostics are supported; reviewed publication status is not established by the supplied arXiv v1 text.
